message.content:
Here’s a quick “how‑to” guide for pulling the comments on **microsoft.com** using your API key (`gamma_key`) and limiting the results to 20 entries.

---

## 1. Endpoint

```
GET https://api.example.com/domains/microsoft.com/comments
```

> Replace `https://api.example.com` with the base URL of the service you’re using.

---

## 2. Query Parameters

| Parameter | Type   | Description                                 | Example |
|-----------|--------|---------------------------------------------|---------|
| `key`     | string | Your API key (used for authentication).     | `gamma_key` |
| `limit`   | int    | Maximum number of comments to return.       | `20` |

> **Tip:** If you need more than 20 comments, you can paginate using `offset` or `page` parameters (check the API docs for exact names).

---

## 3. Full Request (cURL)

```bash
curl -X GET "https://api.example.com/domains/microsoft.com/comments?key=gamma_key&limit=20" \
     -H "Accept: application/json"
```

---

## 4. Full Request (Python `requests`)

```python
import requests

url = "https://api.example.com/domains/microsoft.com/comments"
params = {
    "key": "gamma_key",
    "limit": 20
}

response = requests.get(url, params=params, headers={"Accept": "application/json"})
data = response.json()

print(data)
```

---

## 5. Sample Response

```json
{
  "domain": "microsoft.com",
  "total_comments": 125,
  "returned": 20,
  "comments": [
    {
      "id": "cmt_001",
      "author": "alice@example.com",
      "timestamp": "2024-10-01T12:34:56Z",
      "content": "Great product!"
    },
    {
      "id": "cmt_002",
      "author": "bob@example.com",
      "timestamp": "2024-10-02T08:21:13Z",
      "content": "Had some issues with the installation."
    }
    /* ... 18 more comment objects ... */
  ]
}
```

> The actual field names may differ; refer to the API documentation for the exact schema.

---

## 6. Pagination (if needed)

If you want to fetch the next set of comments:

```bash
curl -X GET "https://api.example.com/domains/microsoft.com/comments?key=gamma_key&limit=20&offset=20"
```

or in Python:

```python
params = {"key": "gamma_key", "limit": 20, "offset": 20}
```

---

### Quick Checklist

- ✅ Replace the base URL with the correct one for your service.
- ✅ Use your real API key (`gamma_key`).
- ✅ Set `limit=20` (or any other number you prefer).
- ✅ Handle pagination if you need more than the first 20 comments.

That’s all you need to pull the first 20 comments for `microsoft.com`. Happy coding!
